SPHEREx Sky Tracker is an automated infrared image-differencing pipeline and interactive web application designed to detect moving celestial objects—such as asteroids—and variable sources across multi-epoch NASA SPHEREx Level 2 exposures.

Space-telescope observations are heavily affected by zodiacal light glow, cosmic-ray hits, and pointing offsets between scans. Our pipeline addresses this by subtracting native ZODI background layers, masking detector artifacts via quality FLAGS, and reprojecting multi-epoch FITS frames onto a unified World Coordinate System (WCS) grid with sub-pixel precision. A four-layer morphological and Point Spread Function (PSF) filter removes cosmic-ray spikes and subtraction dipoles, while time-series interpolation and parallel SIMBAD catalog cross-matching separate known static stars from uncataloged moving candidates.

By transforming SPHEREx's all-sky near-infrared survey data into an accessible, reproducible detection workflow with exportable astrometry, this tool accelerates asteroid discovery, planetary defense monitoring, and transient astrophysics.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

SPHEREx Sky Tracker is an automated infrared image-differencing pipeline and interactive web application designed to detect moving celestial objects (such as asteroids) and variable sources across multi-epoch NASA SPHEREx Level 2 exposures (T1, T2).

1. Level 2 Pre-processing: Subtracts native zodiacal background emission (ZODI) and masks cosmic-ray hits and detector artifacts using quality bitmasks (FLAGS bits 0–19).

2. Two-Step Sub-Pixel WCS Alignment: Reprojects epoch T2 onto the T1 World Coordinate System (WCS) grid with sub-pixel registration refinement (achieving a 0.35 px alignment residual) and median aperture flux normalization.

3. Four-Layer Morphological & PSF Filtering: At a default 9.0-sigma threshold, the pipeline removes linear satellite trails, flat/elongated artifacts, sub-3-pixel cosmic-ray spikes, and subtraction dipoles while validating candidates against the empirical Point Spread Function (PSF).

4. Time Interpolation & Parallel SIMBAD Cross-Matching: Reconstructs linear trajectories across the 42.3-hour baseline and queries the SIMBAD astronomical database concurrently (30-arcsec search radius) to separate known static stars (e.g., filtering out halo-edge false positive Cand-X1) from uncataloged moving candidates (e.g., asteroid candidate Cand-X8).

Benefits & Intended Impact

By transforming complex multi-epoch near-infrared survey FITS files into an accessible visual workflow with one-click CSV astrometry export, SPHEREx Sky Tracker accelerates asteroid discovery, planetary defense monitoring, and transient astrophysics research.

Tools, Languages & Software Stack

- Language & Web Framework: Python, Streamlit (deployed on Streamlit Community Cloud)

- Astronomy & Scientific Libraries: Astropy, reproject, astroquery (SIMBAD), NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib

- Data Sources: NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) SPHEREx Level 2 FITS products and the CDS SIMBAD catalog

Creativity & Engineering Considerations

Instead of relying solely on raw pixel subtraction—which produces thousands of false positives from cosmic rays and bright-star halos—our team combined empirical PSF validation with automated parallel SIMBAD cross-matching. We also optimized FITS array memory management so the full alignment and differencing pipeline runs reliably within a 1 GB cloud RAM limit.

Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure

Generative AI assistants (Google Gemini, Antigravity IDE and Anthropic Claude) were used strictly for Python/Streamlit coding, debugging, UI styling, and English documentation editing. All astrophysics algorithms, data processing logic, and candidate validations were designed and verified by Team 10LY2NHUEr.
